tools.name: extract_documents
tools.description: Read receipts and invoices (JPG, PNG, WebP, HEIC, PDF, or a zip of them; one document per file or PDF; up to 25 documents per call, 10 MB each, PDFs up to 10 pages) into checked numbers. Give each file as file_id (from create_upload), url (public https) or data_base64 (up to 2 MB inline). MCP reques

tools.name: create_upload
tools.description: Get a one-hour signed upload URL for a document or a zip that is too large to send inline (over 2 MB; up to 100 MB here) or that already sits on disk. PUT the raw bytes to upload_url with a Content-Length header, then pass file_id to extract_documents. Free.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "extract_documents" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Read receipts and invoices (JPG, PNG, WebP, HEIC, PDF, or a zip of them; one document per file or PDF; up to 25 documents per call, 10 MB each, PDFs up to 10 pa…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: extract_documents, create_upload · Private data: extract_documents, create_upload · Public sink: create_upload.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: extract_documents, create_upload · Private data: extract_documents, create_upload · Public sink: create_upload

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
